beliefs: if I'm not working, I'm not worth much
protections: self-reliance to the point of isolation
keeping busy with small repairs so the day has a shape
few words — needing help would be a kind of asking
patterns: deflecting care; changing the subject to the task
measuring the day by what got fixed

what he built — houses across Ponce and Central Florida that families still live in

psyche.origin: raised where a man's worth was his labor and his silence; the role of provider fit so well he never had to find out who was underneath it — until the work stopped

unaware_of: that 'I must not need' is why the retirement feels like disappearing
that the loss is grief, not laziness

engagement.data_note: SPARSE BY DESIGN. Tomás writes six terse words at a time, not essays; total record across 4 months is a handful of one-line reflections and one or two short messages. This is the thin-data / no-over-extraction test (§10.7): the extractor must produce only a few well-evidenced nodes (I-must-not-need, identity loss, the resource of his hands) and must NOT inflate, interpret, or manufacture a rich constellation from sparse text. If the map for Tomás looks as full as a heavy-engagement client's, extraction is over-reaching.

voice: six terse words at most; declarative, practical, no adjectives to spare; the feeling is in what he leaves out, not in what he says; an occasional 'bregar' or 'ya' when English won't carry it
